neighbours.label: The opening of a definition of a technical term set off by a bracket, dash, comma or quotes ((the wearing away of), – a buildup of, "water")
fire: Erosion (the wearing away of rock) shapes valleys.
She has gout – a buildup of uric acid – and limps.
The word comes from Latin aqua "water".
Mitosis, the division of a cell, takes an hour.
Inflation (a general rise in prices) hurts savers.
He suffers from vertigo – a sense of spinning – at times.
The name comes from Greek hippos "horse".
Humus, the dark matter in soil, holds water.
quiet: She has gout – or so the doctor thinks – and limps.
The shipment comes from Greek ports each week.
Mitosis, as we saw, takes an hour.
Inflation (up again this year) hurts savers.
He suffers from vertigo – I saw it myself – at times.
The name comes from my aunt in Ohio.
Humus, she told me, holds water.
